races.name: Thank You GRP Solutions For Sponsoring Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Chasing Time
runners_data.note: Lightly raced debutant from powerful Charlie Appleby stable with excellent breeding for middle distances but completely unproven.
runners_data.comment: Dam a Group-placed 1m1f winner (RPR 104); yard always feared in these races
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth foal of a French Group-placed 1m1f winner (RPR 104), herself a sister to Group-placed 1m winner Flowrider; gelded prior to debut; stable always command huge respect in AW maiden/novice events.

runners_data.name: Sinocentric
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who was green and inexperienced on debut 24 days ago, bred to improve but faces pace disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Modest fourth of six on last month's debut but bred to leave that behind him in time
runners_data.spotlight: In need of the experience when fourth of six, beaten 9.5l, in a 1m4f novice at Southwell 24 days ago; bred to do much better at some point.

runners_data.name: Killer Whale
runners_data.note: Front-running type who can control the pace from the start but hasn't run for 115 days and stamina over 1m4f remains unproven.
runners_data.comment: Modest form in two 1m runs in late 2025; dam a Cesarewitch winner so new trip looks a plus
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form in two 1m AW runs in late 2025, finishing a 6l second behind an exciting stablemate of Chasing Time at Kempton in December; out of a Cesarewitch winner so the step up in trip should suit.

races.paceDynamic: Killer Whale will be the uncontested leader from the start, setting a sustainable gallop with no pressure from the other two runners. Chasing Time, despite being lightly raced, is bred for middle distances and will likely settle behind the pace, while Sinocentric's hold-up style means he'll track last. The absence of early pace pressure creates a tactical race where the front-runner can dictate terms completely. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can control the tempo, giving Killer Whale a significant tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Killer Whale Wires All
scenarios.trigger: If Killer Whale gets an uncontested lead and maintains stamina over 1m4f
scenarios.body: The gelding can dictate a comfortable pace and has enough tactical speed to resist late challenges. His prominent style perfectly suits controlling this small field from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Appleby Newcomer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Chasing Time shows the natural ability his breeding suggests on debut
scenarios.body: The Charlie Appleby-trained debutant can settle behind Killer Whale and use superior class to sweep past in the final furlong. Appleby's strike rate with well-bred newcomers makes this a serious threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Decisive
scenarios.trigger: If the 1m4f distance finds out Killer Whale's stamina reserves late on
scenarios.body: Killer Whale leads but weakens in the final quarter-mile, allowing the more proven stayers to pick up the pieces. Sinocentric's hold-up style could benefit from a true staying test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If all three runners show stamina limitations or inexperience over the trip
scenarios.body: The race becomes a crawl with all three struggling for home, creating an unpredictable finish where any of the trio could prevail. Form lines become irrelevant in such circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Killer Whale breaks alertly and establishes an early lead as he could steal a march on inexperienced rivals
Monitor Chasing Time's market moves as Appleby newcomers often attract smart money when ready to win
Observe how Sinocentric settles early as his hold-up style needs the leaders to go too fast to be effective
Check if any of the three show signs of greenness or inexperience over this longer trip as all have limited experience
Watch for tactical positioning in the back straight as the small field could create a stop-start gallop

races.name: In Remembrance Of Aggrey Burke Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Poetic Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with proven C&D winning form who benefits from modest pace scenarios and retains Myla Coppins who partnered his last victory here
runners_data.comment: C&D winner in February; one good run and one lesser effort have followed
runners_data.spotlight: Recorded the 18th win of his long career when leading late over C&D in February (for Myla Coppins); ran well behind a thriving rival at Lingfield next time but he failed to fire over C&D a fortnight ago (finished behind Coloane); he has bounced back from quiet runs before so can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Yehudi
runners_data.note: Prominent runner likely to lead but 0-15 record and inexperienced 7lb claimer Hope Regan are concerns despite going close over C&D previously
runners_data.comment: 0-15 but has gone close, including over C&D; new combination of accessories tried today
runners_data.spotlight: 0-15 but he has gone close on occasions, including over C&D in December; another new combination of accessories tried this afternoon; inexperienced apprentice booked.

runners_data.name: Coloane
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare showing promising signs on return from long break with valuable 3lb claimer Conor Whiteley reducing her to an attractive racing weight
runners_data.comment: Promising run after a break here two weeks ago; shouldn't be too far away
runners_data.spotlight: Infrequent winner but she made a promising return from a 108-day break here two weeks ago; talented claimer takes off a valuable 3lb; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Orbital Chime
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner struggling since stable switch with stewards' attention for previous behavior raising tactical questions under Harry Vigors
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in two 7f runs for new yard; down in weights; first run over further than 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins over 6f for previous trainers; unplaced in two runs for new stable (7f), catching the attention of the stewards on the first occasion, and hopes appear to rest on this first attempt at further than 7f having a positive effect.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who threw away winning chance over C&D in February but form has declined since and needs to rediscover that level
runners_data.comment: Second over C&D in February, when rather throwing the race away; not so good twice since
runners_data.spotlight: Hung away a winning opportunity over C&D in February and neither run since has been as good; more minor money perhaps his best hope.

runners_data.name: Always Fearless
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran with solid C&D winning form last time who reportedly traveled poorly at Lingfield but capable of bouncing back here
runners_data.comment: C&D win last month was followed by a modest run at Lingfield; capable of bouncing back
runners_data.spotlight: Readily saw off eight rivals over C&D last month; reportedly never travelled when disappointing at Lingfield since; capable of bouncing back in this field.

runners_data.name: Not So Sobers
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making Flat debut after hurdling career with 37-day break since last run potentially leaving him short of peak fitness
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on the Flat and ran well last time but that was 1m6f; drop in trip the query
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner and a fair maiden hurdler; didn't achieve much in his first four Flat runs but he was sent off favourite for a 1m6f handicap at Chelmsford in February and plugged on for a close third; can do better in this sphere but dropping back to 8.6f not sure to suit.

runners_data.name: Nala The Lioness
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who is an 11-race maiden struggling badly for new stable after 400-day absence and faces difficult task off bottom weight
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in two handicaps for new yard after a 400-day layoff; plenty to prove
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden; sent off at big odds and well beaten in two runs for new stable after a 400-day absence; down in trip/weights but has a point to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Yehudi will take the field along from the front with his prominent style, but at a controlled tempo given no other confirmed pace angles in this field. The lack of early pressure means the pace will be steady rather than strong, allowing the large contingent of hold-up horses including Poetic Force, Coloane, Always Fearless, and Book Of Life to get into comfortable stalking positions. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses and late runners who can capitalize on the modest gallop and kick late over this 1m2f trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Suits Veterans
scenarios.trigger: If Yehudi sets an uncontested lead and the pace stays moderate throughout
scenarios.body: The experienced campaigners Poetic Force and Always Fearless can time their challenges perfectly from off the pace. Both have proven C&D form and the tactical nous to exploit a slow-run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Yehudi gets away with soft fractions and the hold-up brigade leave their runs too late
scenarios.body: The Mark Loughnane runner capitalizes on loose rein racing to build an unassailable advantage. His stamina holds under minimal pressure despite apprentice Hope Regan's inexperience.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Improving Filly Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Coloane's promising return run proves she's back to her best after the 108-day break
scenarios.body: Roger Fell's mare benefits from the strongly-run pace her hold-up style demands and Conor Whiteley's 3lb claim. Her recent fourth suggests she's found form again at the right time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo becomes pedestrian and multiple hold-up horses converge simultaneously in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where any of the closers could prevail on the day. Orbital Chime or Book Of Life could sneak through if the favorites falter.

watchPoints.text: Yehudi could steal this if Hope Regan manages fractions properly and the field gives him too much rope in the early stages
Always Fearless traveled poorly last time at Lingfield so monitor his early positioning and whether he settles kindly for Tyrese Cameron
Orbital Chime has attracted stewards' attention recently so watch for any signs of reluctance or hanging during the race
Coloane's return to form signs will be evident early if she travels smoothly into contention for Conor Whiteley after her encouraging recent fourth
Poetic Force's veteran instincts and Myla Coppins' partnership could prove decisive if they time their run perfectly from their customary hold-up position

races.name: Remembrance Of Ferdinand Addo Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C & D) (GBB)

runners_data.name: Constant Star
runners_data.note: Only front runner in field, gets uncontested lead but 30 days since last run could blunt finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Promising 2nd in a slowly-run 1m maiden last month; open to plenty of improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Promising debut when second of seven in a slowly-run 1m maiden at Lingfield last month; open to plenty of improvement and he is high on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Imelda
runners_data.note: Unraced newcomer from powerful Loughnane stable, complete unknown but breeding suggests ability over this trip
runners_data.comment: Half-sister to a 1m4f AW winner; she doesn't have a daunting standard to aim at on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 17,000gns yearling; third foal; half-sister to 1m4f AW winner Nancy P (RPR 67); unraced dam closely related to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner Nations Alexander; doesn't have a daunting standard to aim at on debut.

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Hold-up style disadvantaged by likely slow pace, but tongue-tie first time and extra furlong may help
runners_data.comment: Modest debut effort last month but the new trip/tongue tie should have a positive effect
runners_data.spotlight: Low-key debut effort when finishing last of the four runners in a 6f fillies' novice at Kempton 17 days ago; new trip/tongue tie can prompt improvement.

runners_data.name: Rogue Desire
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 233-day layoff, will need serious pace collapse to be competitive from rear
runners_data.comment: Satisfactory debut when third at Salisbury (7f) last August; open to improvement this year
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off the 7-2 third favourite for her Salisbury debut (7f, good to firm) last August but she was unable to land a telling blow, beaten 4.5l into third at the finish; bred to do better at some point.

runners_data.name: Thimble
runners_data.note: Hold-up style and wants longer trips according to pedigree, 45 days off and wrong race shape
runners_data.comment: Bred for further but February's Kempton debut (7f) wasn't without encouragement
runners_data.spotlight: Pedigree suggests she is unlikely to come into her own until tackling 1m2f+ but she did shape with some promise at Kempton in February, only weakening in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Action Reaction
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner disadvantaged by dropping back to 7f from recent 1m efforts
runners_data.comment: Modest form in two 1m runs last month; handicaps should offer a better opportunity
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form in her two 1m runs last month, albeit the second effort represented improvement; drop to 7f not sure to suit on pedigree.

runners_data.name: Safe Zone
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but has shown best form over 6f here, extra furlong should suit and track knowledge helps
runners_data.comment: Some promise in two 6f runs and this extra furlong should suit; each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: She has displayed some ability in her two 6f runs here this year and should prove better suited by today's extra furlong; has more to offer.

runners_data.name: Difford Girl
runners_data.note: Tailed off last time and completely outclassed, 4-year-old carrying penalty weight
runners_data.comment: 66-1 when tailed off in a 9.4f novice here three weeks ago; can't be recommended
runners_data.spotlight: 66-1 when tailed off in a 9.4f novice here three weeks ago; can't be recommended.

races.paceDynamic: Constant Star is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead from the gates. With most runners showing hold-up tendencies (Rogue Desire, Thimble, Action Reaction, Safe Zone, Difford Girl), there's no early pace pressure expected. This sets up a tactical affair where the pace-setter controls the tempo completely. This race shape heavily favours prominent runners and those that can travel close to the pace early, as the lack of early speed will create a sprint finish that disadvantages pure hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Constant Star maintains a controlled gallop and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The front runner faces no early pressure and dictates ideal fractions before finding extra when challenged. Hold-up horses face an impossible task from too far back in a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a pure sprint finish
scenarios.body: The glacial early tempo allows one hold-up horse with superior finishing kick to reel in the leaders. Class and raw ability overcome poor positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Constant Star sets reasonable fractions and gets joined by another forward runner
scenarios.body: A more genuine pace develops with 2-3 horses racing prominently throughout. The horse tracking the leader in second or third position proves best positioned for the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Constant Star goes impossibly slow and field bunches up completely
scenarios.body: The race becomes a 2-furlong dash where positioning means nothing and pure speed wins. The horse with the highest finishing kick from anywhere in the field takes it.

watchPoints.text: Constant Star must be watched for early pace - if he goes too slow it creates impossible tactical scenario for most field
Imelda's market support crucial as stable debut runners can be well-backed when ready to win first time
Safe Zone's early positioning critical - needs to be closer than usual hold-up style to cope with likely slow pace
Thai Princess with new tongue-tie and extra furlong could show marked improvement from poor Kempton debut
Late money moves on any hold-up runners like Rogue Desire or Thimble would suggest pace collapse expected

races.name: Thank You Opus Foundation Handicap

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with most ability in the field despite poor win record, needs pace collapse to be effective from rear
runners_data.comment: Well up to winning off this mark and found only a flourishing rival too strong last week
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win to his name after 21 starts but he has a lot of ability for one racing at this level and he found only the flourishing Yorkshire Glory too strong at Newcastle last week; 1lb rise negligible and obvious claims, for all he looks one to tread carefully with at short prices.

runners_data.name: Kirkdale
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type seeking first handicap win, can miss break but solid recent 6f form gives him claims
runners_data.comment: Four solid efforts since dropped to 6f; the start is an issue but solid form claims
runners_data.spotlight: Still seeking his first handicap success but he has run creditably in four starts since dropping back to 6f; can miss the break but he has solid form claims otherwise.

runners_data.name: Lequinto
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse slipping down weights, needs strong pace to unleash his finishing kick effectively
runners_data.comment: No AW win since December 2021; arrives in fair form though and he has an each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: No AW win since December 2021 but there have been some good runs on both Polytrack and Tapeta this year; slipping down the weights and he holds each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Pianoforte
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner trying cheekpieces for first time, hasn't built on December fourth and needs everything to fall right
runners_data.comment: Promising 4th in December but he hasn't built on it since; now tried in cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Should be well handicapped now but he hasn't built on a good fourth at Newcastle in December in three subsequent runs; connections reach for cheekpieces tonight.

runners_data.name: Punchbowl Flyer
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning to preferred 6f trip, solid recent efforts but only one win since 2021
runners_data.comment: Just one win since June 2021 but he has been performing with credit in defeat this year
runners_data.spotlight: Series of creditable efforts this year and returning to 6f is no bad thing; only one win to his name since June 2021 though.

runners_data.name: Brian The Snail
runners_data.note: Slow-starting veteran having 100th career start, recent Newcastle fourth was encouraging for patient tactics
runners_data.comment: Having his 100th racecourse start tonight; solid 4th last time; each-way claims once again
runners_data.spotlight: Slow-starting veteran who is having his 100th outing this evening; he has won 14 times already and his latest Newcastle fourth was a solid effort; should go well again.

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing improvement for new yard after Kempton second, runs off same mark as that effort
runners_data.comment: 0-20 but latest 2nd was a solid effort; new combination of accessories; contender
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17 when trained by Charles Hills and beaten on in three runs for new stable too, albeit his latest second at Kempton was much more encouraging; runs off the same mark today and a tongue tie and cheekpieces are worn together today (worn independently in the past).

runners_data.name: Due Date
runners_data.note: Front-runner with four wins in purple patch last year, struggling this season and has plenty to prove now
runners_data.comment: Had a good 2025 campaign but well beaten at big odds in three runs this year
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins in a purple patch in the second half of 2025; struggled at big odds in three runs this year; enough to prove for now.

runners_data.name: Megaphone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has declined since yard switch, no sign of revival and unlikely to reverse form
runners_data.comment: Tumbling down the weights but showing no sign of taking advantage
runners_data.spotlight: Went the wrong way for George Boughey last year and no sign of a revival for new yard this winter.

races.paceDynamic: Due Date and Punchbowl Flyer will contest the early lead in this small field, with both confirmed front-runners likely to set an honest gallop over this sharp 6f trip. The pace should be solid rather than frantic given only two genuine speed horses, creating a race that unfolds in straight lines without dramatic tempo changes. With seven of nine runners holding-up types, there's limited early speed beyond the two leaders, meaning they can dictate without being harassed. This moderate pace scenario clearly favours the prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can sit close, as the hold-up horses face a wall of traffic in a small field sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Dictate Terms
scenarios.trigger: If Due Date and Punchbowl Flyer are allowed to bowl along unchallenged through steady fractions
scenarios.body: The pace will be just fast enough to blunt the finishing kicks of the hold-up brigade, while the two leaders can battle it out in the straight. Those racing prominently behind them get first run at the leaders when they tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes pedestrian with the leaders going too slowly
scenarios.body: This creates a sprint finish where the superior class horses can unleash devastating late runs through the field. The patient tactics of the better-rated hold-up horses will be perfectly suited to this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses gets prominent early positioning behind the leaders
scenarios.body: They can stalk the pace and have the perfect trip to strike when the front two weaken. This suits horses that can adapt their running style and get good positioning in small fields.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders stop quickly after setting unsustainable fractions
scenarios.body: The race becomes a mad dash from the back with multiple hold-up horses converging on the line. This chaotic finish could produce a surprise winner from the rear ranks.

watchPoints.text: Watch Due Date's early fractions - if he goes off too fast he could collapse and set up the hold-up horses perfectly
Monitor Kirkdale at the start as he can miss the break badly which would be fatal in a small sprint field
Check if Brian The Snail gets his usual slow start as the veteran needs to be closer in this small field
Observe Punchbowl Flyer's positioning - if he lets Due Date lead alone he might get a better tactical trip
Watch for Cayman Tai getting a clear run in the straight as he has the most natural ability despite poor strike rate

races.name: Thank You To Omari For The Support Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Maasai Mara
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 595 days off with first-time hood replacing cheekpieces, hard to assess after such a long layoff
runners_data.comment: Lost his way over hurdles; hard to believe he's still up to this sort of mark on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Lost his way over hurdles, running poorly in two runs back from a break last November; the usual cheekpieces are replaced by a first-time hood and it's hard to believe he's still up to this sort of mark on the Flat.

runners_data.name: Codiak
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up type in excellent recent form with strong AW record, but needs others to set up the race
runners_data.comment: Came from off a steady pace to get up in a busy finish last time; open to more improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't need to improve to win an uncompetitive C&D novice in the winter but did it impressively and he bettered that at Southwell (off 2lb lower than today) next time, coming from off a steady pace to get up in a busy finish; remains open to further improvement.

runners_data.name: Charmaine
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 195-day break, historically performs well fresh but faces revised handicap mark
runners_data.comment: Looked to find this mark beyond her after two wins last spring but this less competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Novice win as a 3yo came after four months off, which is a positive as she returns from a six-month absence; looked to find this sort of mark just beyond her after two victories last spring (Tapeta, Polytrack) but this is less competitive.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Donegal
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner wearing first-time visor, proven at C&D and likely to get uncontested lead
runners_data.comment: Made all in a first-time visor over C&D five weeks ago; a 4lb rise demands more
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent in defeat all winter and the combination of a first-time visor and uncontested lead was enough to get him back to winning ways over C&D five weeks ago; a 4lb rise demands more.

runners_data.name: Polling Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse aged 8 returning from 203 days off, entitled to need the run at his age
runners_data.comment: Entitled to need this at his age after seven months off; trainer also runs Bulldog Spirit
runners_data.spotlight: Soft-ground win last summer came off a 4lb lower mark and he's entitled to need this at his age back from seven months off; trainer also saddles Bulldog Spirit.

runners_data.name: Bulldog Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer joining fourth different yard, has shown ability to win fresh but long absence
runners_data.comment: Debuts for a fourth yard; not much room for manoeuvre off this mark on comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Debuts for a fourth yard having been picked up from Brian Ellison last autumn for 7,500gns; won first time out as a 2yo and on his comeback last spring, which gives hope, but there's not much room for manoeuvre off this mark.

runners_data.name: Gemmari
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good recent form with strong AW record, but revised mark makes task harder
runners_data.comment: Helped set the race up when favourite here last time; has to prove this mark within range
runners_data.spotlight: Helped set the race up for the closers when favourite here last time, having previously won easily over 1m6f round Chelmsford; now has to prove his revised mark is within range coming back down in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Pride Of Donegal will get an uncontested lead with only one other confirmed front runner absent, allowing him to dictate terms from the front. Bulldog Spirit may provide some early company from a prominent position, but the pace will be manageable rather than fierce. The sustained gallop over 1m4f will stretch the field out, with the hold-up horses (Maasai Mara, Codiak, Charmaine, Polling Day, Gemmari) needing to make ground from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the traffic problems that will hamper the large contingent of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Pride Of Donegal gets his preferred soft lead and maintains it
scenarios.body: The uncontested pace allows him to save energy for a sustained kick, making it difficult for hold-up horses to peg him back. His recent C&D win in similar circumstances with the visor makes him hard to oppose.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Hold-Up Horse Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly searching or Pride Of Donegal stops quickly
scenarios.body: Codiak or Charmaine can use their superior class ratings to sweep past a tiring leader. The higher-rated hold-up horses finally get the race shape they need to unleash their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Pride Of Donegal goes too slow early and multiple horses challenge late
scenarios.body: A bunched finish develops where track position becomes crucial and several hold-up horses get their chance. Gemmari's recent form and proven AW ability could see him sneak through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites underperform or traffic issues arise in running
scenarios.body: Maasai Mara with his first-time hood or a refreshed Polling Day could capitalize on a messy pace scenario. The longer absence horses sometimes spring surprises when others disappoint.

watchPoints.text: Pride Of Donegal getting a soft early lead could make him very hard to peg back given his front-running style and recent C&D success
Codiak and Charmaine may struggle to get competitive if the pace is too slow, as both need strong gallop to show their best
Maasai Mara's first-time hood after 595 days off makes him unpredictable and hard to assess
Bulldog Spirit joining his fourth trainer could be significant given his record of winning fresh for new connections
The large contingent of hold-up horses may create traffic problems in the straight, potentially setting up an outsider

races.name: Founding Member Of ACCI WRPA Handicap

runners_data.name: Blue Force
runners_data.note: Prominent runner drawn well who beat Candy Warhol at this course in December and suits the likely pace scenario despite recent poor form
runners_data.comment: C&D win off this mark in December; unplaced five times since but could revive from stall 1
runners_data.spotlight: Beat Candy Warhol over C&D in December off this mark; unplaced in five runs since but he is well drawn and a revival wouldn't be a huge shock; stable also runs Toomuchforme.

runners_data.name: Beaming Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer dropping to 5f for first time after three career wins came over 1m, making this trip a significant unknown
runners_data.comment: Three wins over 1m; on a good mark but dropping to 5f is an obvious query
runners_data.spotlight: On a competitive mark but his three wins have come over 1m and dropping to 6f didn't help matters ten days ago; now has his first 5f run.

runners_data.name: Candy Warhol
runners_data.note: Front-runner with proven course form who should get uncontested lead but faces horses he's closely matched with on recent running
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; closely matched with Blue Force on December's C&D run; should go well
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won three times at Wolverhampton last year, including at this trip; closely matched with Blue Force on their C&D run in December; sharper for his recent reappearance; stable also runs Phoenix Beach.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Beach
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who hangs right but wasn't beaten far here two weeks ago and suits these exact conditions well
runners_data.comment: Faces his optimum conditions and ran well for third here two weeks ago; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Not straightforward (hangs right) but these conditions suit him well and he wasn't beaten far into third here two weeks ago; one of two contenders for Scott Dixon.

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 177 days absence with poor fresh record despite returning on last winning mark
runners_data.comment: C&D winner and returns on his last winning mark; record fresh points to looking elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Conditions no problem and he returns from an absence on his last winning mark; record fresh doesn't suggest this will be his day though.

runners_data.name: Shalaa Asker
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with three 5f wins this winter, only 1lb worse off for narrow defeat to Toomuchforme last time
runners_data.comment: Three AW wins this winter and also ran well behind Toomuchforme at Southwell last month
runners_data.spotlight: Three 5f wins this winter and he found only Toomuchforme too strong at Southwell last month; 1lb better off for a head defeat; chance.

runners_data.name: Amerjeet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with poor strike-rate on dangerous low mark but hasn't always shown full effort under pressure previously
runners_data.comment: Poor strike-rate but conditions hold no terrors and he is down to a career-low mark
runners_data.spotlight: Poor strike-rate and hasn't always looked the most eager under pressure; conditions no problem and on a dangerous mark so can't rule out another prominent showing.

runners_data.name: Toomuchforme
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing visor who beat Shalaa Asker last time but now 3lb higher and ridden by inexperienced 3lb claimer
runners_data.comment: Revived by visor on last two starts, beating Shalaa Asker at Southwell last month; solid
runners_data.spotlight: Revived by a visor of late, third at Newcastle in February and then getting the better of Shalaa Asker at Southwell 25 days ago; 3lb higher today and the stable also runs Blue Force.

races.paceDynamic: Candy Warhol will lead from the gates with Blue Force and Toomuchforme tracking closely in prominent positions, creating a moderate gallop over this sharp 5f trip. The lone front-runner won't face serious pressure early, allowing him to dictate terms before the inevitable sprint home. Phoenix Beach, Shalaa Asker, Beaming Light and Amerjeet will be held up off the pace, relying on late kicks. This sustainable early pace followed by a fierce final furlong strongly favours prominent runners who can track the leader and kick when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained gallop finish
scenarios.trigger: If Candy Warhol maintains a steady tempo without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The pace will be honest but not frantic, setting up a proper test where prominent runners can position ideally and outkick the leader late. Blue Force and Toomuchforme are perfectly placed to strike from their tracking positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Candy Warhol gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The leader will have enough left in the tank to resist late challenges, particularly given his proven course form and the burden on closers. Phoenix Beach might pick up pieces from his hold-up position but the damage is done.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closer surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with Blue Force or Toomuchforme pressing Candy Warhol
scenarios.body: The front division will come back dramatically in the final 100 yards as stamina tells. Shalaa Asker and Phoenix Beach, both in good current form, will benefit most from this collapse scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Candy Warhol goes too slow and creates a cavalry charge finish
scenarios.body: The entire field will be bunched turning for home, making it a pure speed test where any horse can win. This chaotic finish could suit an outsider like Amerjeet on his dangerous low mark.

watchPoints.text: Candy Warhol could steal this if allowed uncontested fractions given his proven ability to win at this venue
Blue Force revival chances depend entirely on recapturing December form when beating today's main rival Candy Warhol
Beaming Light drops to 5f for first time having won three times over 1m, making this a significant trip experiment
Phoenix Beach's right-handed hanging tendency could cost him vital momentum in the final furlong despite good recent form
Shalaa Asker carries just 1lb penalty for narrow defeat to Toomuchforme and meets that rival on better terms today

races.name: Thank You, Ina Deans Lifelong Carer Handicap

runners_data.name: Amazing Anita
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly showing clear improvement in cheekpieces first time, 31 days fresh should have her sharp for James Fanshawe
runners_data.comment: Closely matched with Karakula Dancer on latest Southwell run; not yet exposed
runners_data.spotlight: 0.75l behind Karakula Dancer when they finished second and third at Southwell last month (1m; cheekpieces first time); open to further progress after just five starts.

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven C&D form, 11-day turnaround could be ideal timing after emphatic last win for in-form Marco Botti
runners_data.comment: Easy C&D win 11 days ago but she was able to dictate; behind two of these on previous run
runners_data.spotlight: Finished behind Karakula Dancer and Amazing Anita at Southwell last month; left that well behind with an emphatic C&D win 11 days ago but she did enjoy the run of the race there and she has an 8lb higher mark to contend with today.

runners_data.name: Karakula Dancer
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong AW handicap record, dual winner who hasn't been seen to best advantage recently but retains clear class edge
runners_data.comment: Two wins and three placed efforts from five AW runs this year; solid claims
runners_data.spotlight: He has turned in a series of good efforts in AW handicaps this year, winning at Lingfield and Kempton (1m) and placed on his other three starts; not seen to best effect when third over C&D 19 days ago and he commands respect.

runners_data.name: Zoustellar
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping up to 1m½f after encouraging Newcastle fourth, Billy Loughnane booking suggests confidence despite modest strike rate
runners_data.comment: Improved effort when unlucky-in-running 4th at Newcastle (1m) last month; unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Ran her best race so far when keeping on for fourth at Newcastle two weeks ago, her first attempt at 1m; she would have finished closer granted a clear run too and she now has something to build on.

runners_data.name: Panthere Noir
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner continuing to drop in weights but recent Newcastle form disappointing, 5lb claimer Ashley Lewis takes valuable weight off
runners_data.comment: Two low-key runs at Newcastle last month; down in the weights but not a solid option
runners_data.spotlight: Two low-key efforts at Newcastle last month (7f); continues to drop down the weights but others bring more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Raspoutine
runners_data.note: Non-runner, 231 days absent makes this a non-entity in the betting calculations
runners_data.comment: Poor form in four 2yo runs at up to 1m; bred for middle distances; betting should guide
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in four runs last summer (7f-1m); unlikely to come into his own until tackling middle-distances but handicap newcomers from the stable can rarely be discounted.

races.paceDynamic: Lexington Express sits as the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the front without pressure in this small field. The prominent runner will face no early challenge, allowing him to control fractions and potentially steal a march on the hold-up brigade behind. With Amazing Anita, Karakula Dancer, Zoustellar and Panthere Noir all needing to be delivered late, they risk getting caught flat-footed if the pace becomes too honest. This race shape strongly favours the early position - either Lexington Express if he can sustain his gallop, or any hold-up horse that can produce a devastating turn of foot when the pace inevitably quickens.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Express maintains his recent C&D winning form and dictates soft fractions early.
scenarios.body: He can use his tactical advantage to build an unassailable lead, making life difficult for the closers who need a stronger pace to aim at. His 11-day turnaround and proven course form give him every chance to exploit this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses can overcome the tactical disadvantage and produce their finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: Karakula Dancer's proven AW handicap form and dual winner status make him the most likely to bridge the gap, while Amazing Anita showed clear improvement last time. The pace may not be strong enough to fully suit their styles but class could tell.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Improving Third Year
scenarios.trigger: If Zoustellar builds on her promising Newcastle fourth and handles the step up to 1m½f.
scenarios.body: Her best effort came at 1m and the extra half-furlong should suit her hold-up style, while Billy Loughnane's booking suggests connections are confident. She represents the each-way angle if the pace develops favorably.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Express fails to handle the step back up in trip or the 11-day turnaround tells.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair with no true pace, allowing an outsider like Panthere Noir to benefit from the drop in weights. This scenario requires multiple favorites to underperform simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Lexington Express dictating easy fractions early - if he's allowed an uncontested lead, the hold-up horses may have too much ground to make up
Amazing Anita's early position - if she gets further back than usual, her hold-up style becomes even more compromised in this pace scenario
Karakula Dancer's jump from the gates - needs to be closer than usual to his rivals given the likely lack of pace up front
Zoustellar handling the step up to 1m½f for the first time - any signs of not staying could end her chances quickly
The pace after the first two furlongs - if it's genuinely soft, this becomes Lexington Express's race to lose
